Machine learning by region: Europe reaches $132B by 2031, behind Asia and North America

Machine learning, the branch of artificial intelligence that learns from data, keeps growing everywhere in the world. But not every region starts from the same level. Statista Market Insights forecasts by region, published in 2026, make it possible to place Europe precisely.

We have already covered the global trajectory of this market in our article on machine learning as the dominant AI segment. The angle here is different: comparing regions with each other, and understanding what that means for a European company choosing its tools.

Three blocs, three starting points

In 2025, Asia is the largest regional machine learning market at about $38.8 billion, followed by North America ($34.3 billion) and Europe ($24.8 billion). Far behind come Latin America ($5.2 billion), Oceania ($2.0 billion) and Africa ($1.9 billion).

By 2031, according to the forecasts, Asia would reach $209.5 billion, North America $187.3 billion and Europe $131.7 billion. The order does not change: Europe stays third, with a market a little under two thirds the size of Asia's.

A useful clarification: these regional series come from a different Statista statistic than the one used in our global market article. Their sum does not match the worldwide total quoted elsewhere; they should be read as a comparison between regions.

The same pace, not the same starting point

The most interesting point lies elsewhere. Between 2025 and 2031, the European market would grow 5.3-fold. That is almost exactly the same multiplier as Latin America, Oceania or Africa, and barely lower than Asia and North America (about 5.4x and 5.5x).

In other words, Europe is not falling behind in speed. It keeps a size gap inherited from a lower starting point. In 2020, its market was already worth about $12.5 billion, compared with $18.2 billion for Asia and $15.1 billion for North America.

That initial gap holds in relative terms throughout the period. In absolute terms, it widens: at the same pace, the largest region adds more billions every year.

A peak in 2021, then a drop in 2022

The source series has one feature that is visible in the chart: every region shows a peak in 2021, followed by a sharp drop in 2022, before recovering from 2023. In Europe, the market goes from about $30.5 billion in 2021 to $16.2 billion in 2022.

This movement appears as such in the published data. We mention it without interpreting it: the source gives no detailed explanation, and what matters for our purpose is the trend from 2023 to 2031 and the gaps between regions.

Why tool hosting becomes a criterion

For a European company, these numbers raise a practical question. If most machine learning capacity develops in Asia and North America, a large share of available tools will be designed and hosted outside Europe.

Yet the data feeding these tools is often sensitive: customer conversations, complaints, call recordings, emails. Processing it falls under the GDPR, and where it is stored is not a legal detail. It is a selection criterion just like performance or price.

Choosing a tool hosted in Europe lets a company benefit from the growth of machine learning without exposing its customers' data to different legal frameworks.

What it changes for customer feedback analysis

One of the most direct business uses of machine learning is automatic language analysis: reading reviews, tickets or call transcripts to extract topics, emotions and signs of dissatisfaction. This kind of use does not require a team of data scientists; it requires clean data and the right tool.

The models involved can be Mistral, BERT, Llama, GPT or Claude depending on the case. For a European company, the challenge is to benefit from these models while keeping control over where its data is processed and how it is used.

It is also a matter of trust with customers themselves, who are increasingly attentive to what happens to their messages.

In practice, this means asking simple questions before signing up for any tool: where are conversations stored, who can access them, are they used to improve the provider's models, and can they be deleted on request? The answers say a lot about how seriously a provider takes customer data.

What this means for you

Europe is growing at the same pace as other regions in machine learning, from a lower base. For your customer data, choosing a tool hosted in Europe matters as much as its performance. custovox.ai is hosted in France, and your data is never used to train models.
